newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds forge ahead, seen supported.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds forge ahead, seen supported.

text.p: German Bunds and futures resumed their determined upward march on Wednesday, driven higher by strong domestic buying power and supportive U.S. Treasuries.

Analysts said that with trade more active than in previous sessions, Wednesday's rally appeared to have a relatively good base, although they could not rule out the possibility of a near-term set back for the market to consolidate.
"The volumes have been signficantly higher than on previous days," said Dirk Aufderheide at DMG Futures & Options in Frankfurt.

By 1440 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was trading 18 basis points higher on the day at 102.91, well off the day's fresh contract high of 103.15 but holding very comfortably above support in the 102.59 region.

A close below the psychological significant 103.00 level might increase the risk of the recent rally petering out, analysts said, while a successful close above this level would offer a further upside target of 103.31.
Bears would only start to be reawakened in the short term of the contract were to close below 102.92 -- the old contract high on September Bunds.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 103.35 for a bid yield of 5.545 percent by 1506 GMT.
Analysts said firmer U.S. Treasuries, which moved to early session highs after wholesale inventories data, were adding to the positive sentiment in the German market.
On spreads, the U.S. market was beginning to outpace Germany by late European trade with the 10-year yield spread squeezing in to 81 basis points from 84 earlier in the day.
